title: Dedicated autoscaler: burst smoothing, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting optimizations
author: Evan Park
description: Motivation: customers using Dedicated fleets saw short-lived spikes exhaust burst tokens and create head-of-line queueing, which degraded p95/p99 latency for latency-sensitive tenants. We need smoother burst behavior, explicit throughput guarantees tied to reserved capacity, and lower-cardinality utilization reporting to make autoscaling decisions and postmortems more reliable.  Summary: this PR implements token-bucket smoothing on the dedicated autoscaler, introduces a throughput-guarantee controller that binds soft throughput targets to a fleet/pool, and refactors utilization reporting to use sampled aggregation and per-pool rollups. Changes are conservative by default (feature gated) and include a gradual rollout plan plus dashboard/alert updates.  What changed (high level): - token-bucket smoothing: new smoothing algorithm in controlplane/autoscaler that replaces instantaneous burst drains with a refill/smoothing window. Allows configurable smoothing_window_ms and refill_rate per-pool. - throughput guarantees: new controller that accepts a ThroughputGuarantee CR (internal API) and enforces a minimum token refill rate for pools that purchase reserved capacity. This ties into billing + SLA checks. - util reporting optimizations: aggregation moved from high-cardinality per-tenant metrics to per-pool sampled counters, with an aux endpoint to reconstruct per-tenant usage for audit when needed. Reduced metric cardinality and cost. - observability: dashboards updated, new alerts for sustained throttle rates and refill failures, and span instrumentation for token acquisition. - tests & docs: unit and integration tests added; docs updated describing config knobs and recommended policies.  Design notes: the smoothing algorithm uses a leaky-bucket abstraction so bursts are consumed at a bounded rate while allowing short spikes. We chose refill-based guarantees rather than hard capped qps to preserve low-latency tail behavior while ensuring predictability for reserved pools. Util reporting uses reservoir sampling for tenants above a cardinality threshold (configurable) to keep Prometheus/Backfill costs under control.  Rollout plan: feature-gated behind feature flag dedicated.autoscaler.smoothing (default off). Rollout steps: (1) enable for 10% of traffic with throughput-guarantee controller off; (2) monitor refill/fail metrics for 48h; (3) enable throughput guarantees for pilot customers; (4) 100% rollout and enable reporting optimizations. Alerts and dashboards are included in this PR to track regressions.  How to review: focus on tokenbucket.go and controller interactions (race conditions), review the util aggregator's sampling correctness, and validate e2e tests that assert p95/p99 under synthetic spike workloads.  Related: ENG-3245, SRE-1120, SUP-4532.

review_comments: Maya Chen: Can we avoid global locks in the tokenbucket implementation? If the aggregator locks per-pool it might become a hotspot.
Author (Evan Park): switched to per-pool sharded mutexes and added comments; included microbenchmarks showing ~2% overhead at 1000 concurrent requests.
Siddharth Singh: Need a clear failure mode if refill fails (e.g., network partition to control plane). How do we degrade gracefully?
Author: added fallback to safe conservative refill rate defined in defaults and emit a dedicated metric dedicated.autoscaler.refill_fallback_count.
Laura Gomez: The change to util reporting reduces cardinality but we should provide a path to request raw per-tenant breakdown for audits.
Author: added an on-demand audit endpoint disabled by default; added RBAC gating and KMS logging note in docs.
ci_checks: benchmarks: microbenchmarks added to perf/canary-suite: pass
release_notes: Added token-bucket smoothing to Dedicated autoscaler to reduce head-of-line queueing during spikes.
Introduced throughput-guarantee controller to bind refill rates to reserved capacity (configurable).
Reduced observability cardinality by sampling utilization reports and added on-demand audit endpoint.
Dashboards and alerts updated for refill failures and sustained throttle rates.
No breaking changes by default; features are feature-gated and off unless enabled in chart values.
merge_outcome: merged after 2 approvals and one round of fixups
notes_for_ops: Enable feature gate 'dedicated.autoscaler.smoothing' in values.yaml (default: false) to test. Watch dedicated.autoscaler.refill_fallback_count and dedicated.autoscaler.throttle_rate. Use the audit endpoint for per-tenant reconstructions (RBAC required).
testing_summary: Unit tests cover tokenbucket edge cases; integration tests simulate bursty traffic and assert p95/p99 improvements; e2e verifies policy rollout. Performance microbenchmarks show ~2% overhead and reduced p99 under synthetic spikes.
security_notes: Audit endpoint gated by RBAC and logged to KMS-backed audit logs; no customer secrets are exported.
